data.narrative: Alekhya demonstrated exceptional distributed systems judgment in Module 07, successfully decoupling redirect execution from analytics writes using Redis and Celery. She implemented atomic storage-level deduplication via ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING, enforced SHA-256 IP hashing for privacy, established owner-scoped analytics with date filters, and swiftly diagnosed an injected idempotency bypass.

dimension_scores.observation: Selected Option B (Asynchronous Queue) with clear justification, accepting eventual consistency for analytics to guarantee bounded redirect latency and availability.
dimension_scores.evidence: Championed Option B: 'When the database has high write latency, the redirect API should continue and return HTTP 302 without waiting for analytics writes.'

dimension_scores.observation: Flawlessly isolated the broken idempotency bug to event ID extraction in the worker without hints.
dimension_scores.evidence: Identified 'event_id = None' in apps/api/app/worker.py and restored 'event_id = event_data.get("event_id")' with atomic conflict handling.

dimension_scores.observation: Strictly upheld user privacy and tenant authorization across all telemetry endpoints.
dimension_scores.evidence: Verified SHA-256 IP hashing (raw IP never persisted) and query-level tenant scoping returning 404 for cross-tenant analytics access.

dimension_scores.observation: Built end-to-end reliability safeguards including graceful degradation on queue outages, automated retry backoff, and 30-day retention purging.
dimension_scores.evidence: Implemented purge_old_clicks maintenance task, graceful queue fallback, and atomic database deduplication passing 50/50 pytest tests.

dimension_scores.observation: Articulated distributed systems principles with exceptional precision and technical depth.
dimension_scores.evidence: Defined idempotency, at-least-once delivery duplicate risks, and queue dead-letter mitigation in clear, structured responses.

strengths: Mature distributed systems instincts: accurately diagnosed at-least-once retry risks and decoupled the redirect hot path.
Flawless debugging methodology: isolated the disarmed idempotency guard directly to worker payload extraction without hints.
Strong production resilience mindset: championed storage-level atomic upserts, graceful degradation, and dead-letter queues.
growth_areas: Ready to explore event streaming and stream processing architectures (e.g. Kafka or Redis Streams consumer groups) for higher throughput.
Ready to tackle multi-node deployment strategies and container orchestration in upcoming practitioner modules.
data.recommendation: Continue building on this distributed async foundation as we advance to containerization and deployment architecture.

public_evidence.artifact: Decoupled Click Analytics Queue & Idempotent Worker
public_evidence.student_action: Engineered asynchronous click event ingestion using Celery and Redis with atomic ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING deduplication, privacy-safe SHA-256 IP hashing, and 30-day retention purging.
public_evidence.proof: Passed 50/50 pytest suite; live verification confirmed 2 redirects queued and processed by Celery worker into PostgreSQL, duplicate job replay returned duplicate_skipped with 1 row in DB, and redirect returned 302 during broker outage.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Proves ability to decouple high-frequency hot paths from telemetry writes using message queues, guarantee at-least-once idempotency at the database layer, enforce data privacy, and ensure graceful service degradation.
